doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

chapter: Staying in Rome and best and worst gigs
title: Playing the Savoy and handling requests
summary: The two-minute commute to the Savoy, and Rowe's and Montalbano's attitude toward requests: it only bothers them not to know the tune.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: And also, did you ever go to your gig at the Savoy and say, “you know what, it just took me three minutes to get here and I don’t have to unload and go park the car.”
Actually it’s two minutes and 45 seconds from door to door. And if I can’t park exactly in front of the place I’m bugged. If I have to park like 20 yards away, that’s it, I’m bugged the whole night.
It’s not a bad place to be, really. It’s not.
No. It’s not. I had someone say to me once “how can you do those piano gigs? Doesn’t it bug you when people come up and ask for songs?” Well no man. It bugs me if I don’t know them.
But, you know, I don’t mind playing “My Way” you just play it good and then you feel okay about it.
I’m the same way. If I don’t know a tune I’m so bugged with myself.
